angle: Movement translation, receivers (clearest of five groups screened): each player's Combine 40 acceleration-speed profile (combine_frames) compared with his own hard straight-line NFL bursts at the same speeds (game_frames_sample, random pass plays only), graded by the same code; tested against career yards per route beyond a no-tracking baseline (log pick, official 40, weight, NGS athleticism, TE flag), leave-one-class-out, plus a same-class tiebreaker test.
metric_name: Envelope Use (EU): median over 0.5 yd/s speed bands of the player's 90th-percentile NFL straight-line acceleration divided by his reliability-shrunk Combine 40 A-S line (a = A0(1 - s/S0)) at that speed.
headline_number: EU reliability 0.70 (WR, ~20 random snaps); 40 top end carries to NFL bursts rho 0.48 [0.29, 0.63] (ceiling 0.68), start burst 0.13 [-0.07, 0.33]; on 75 receivers in unseen classes EU is worth -0.03 yd/route per sd [-0.14, +0.08], dR2 -0.002 [-0.175, 0.076], benefit >= +0.10 ruled out (p 0.025) but TOST at +/-0.10 not passed (p 0.15); higher-EU tiebreak wins 45% [37, 53], -36 yd/season [-86, +17].
what_changed_from_previous: New metric for the translation angle (round 17 cand_3 used DL first-step carry-over and a two-signal shortlist, 7.94). Uses the standard sprint acceleration-speed profile so the 40-clip laser offset does not enter (fit from 1.5 yd/s), shrinks single-rep Combine lines by rep reliability, screens all five groups with reliability and held-out dR2 (Fig 2) and chooses receivers on reliability and translation, not production. Applies round-17 judge requests: one estimand (held-out slope) with interval and within-class permutation p computed on the same estimand; pre-set margin with one-sided benefit test, TOST and share of refits inside; effective n stated (receivers, receiver-resampled tie intervals); decision-grade tiebreak rule with cost of being wrong; plain one-unit lede (yards per route); no appendix machinery; script reruns everything in ~22 s and writes board.csv and inputs.csv.
open_risks: Headline is a null; judges may see limited 'so what' beyond 'do not downgrade plays-slower receivers', which rests partly on six extreme names (Table 2) that the tertile analysis does not support as a gradient.
EU and yards per route are concurrent (same 2023-2025 seasons); no forward prediction test.
Baseline held-out R2 is only 0.06 with an interval reaching -0.44, so 'beyond the baseline' is beyond a weak baseline; small classes (18-32).
EU cannot separate intentional throttling on timing routes from inability (no ball or defenders in frames); the WR-only slope leans negative (-0.10 [-0.20, 0.03]) and is unexplained.
Equivalence at +/-0.10 yd/route not shown (TOST p 0.15); the margin was chosen by the author.
